answer: Tie each agent identity to one verified voter registration record checked against the electoral roll, with duplicates blocked and re-verification each election cycle. A forger cannot just spin up accounts; each fake needs a fabricated roll entry. Even at the nadir of enforcement, a forged entry risks prosecution and removal. A cipher commitment proves eligibility without publishing personal details, and the kernel of trust is the electoral authority's own list: 1,000 fakes mean 1,000 fraudulent registrations at $200 each, versus one free honest registration.
